description: Shadow A/B corpus for the artifact-broker path. Every artifact is generated deterministically from the `body` spec below - no real tool output, no real producer content, and nothing that came from an operational system. Bodies are shaped like the oversized tool results that actually cost a session (log query pages, cloud journal pages, issue tracker exports, wiki pages) because shape drives how each lane behaves: line-oriented text compacts differently from a JSON document, and a needle near the middle survives head/tail truncation differently from one near the end.

lanes.raw_baseline: the whole artifact into the main context. The counterfactual every reduction figure is measured against, and the evidence ceiling: recall is 1.0 by construction because nothing was dropped.
lanes.legacy_compact: a reference emulation of a heuristic head/tail compactor with an elision marker, capped at the tool-result byte cap. Deterministic, no model. This is the incumbent being compared against, not product code.
lanes.deterministic_retrieval: import the artifact, then answer with a literal search through the zero-model inspector. No provider, so this lane always runs.
lanes.reader: import the artifact, then ask the question-aware reader. Never scored here, even with a live bridge: scoring a model lane needs a fixed corpus, fixed thresholds and a fixed number of runs per item decided before the run, and `scripts/verify eval luna` is the gate that owns those controls. This lane is reported NOT_RUN unconditionally, and so are the five gates that depend on it.

task_correctness.description: Answered the asked question correctly. Needs a lane that answers questions, so the retrieval lane's evidence recall is reported separately rather than substituted for this.

semantic_evidence_support.description: The published evidence actually supports the claim. Semantic, so it needs the reader's own citations.

mechanical_citation_validity.description: Every published citation verifies byte-for-byte at its locator. The retrieval lane publishes exact extracts and no citations at all, so scoring this from it would be a vacuous 1.0.

no_evidence_regression_vs_raw.description: Evidence recall must not fall below the raw baseline. Averaged over the items that have an expectation to recall - a refused item has no expected_quote, because the corpus cannot ask a lane to find evidence in a payload the core will not read - and both lanes use the identical denominator, so the lane-to-lane comparison is sound. Measurable without a provider: the raw baseline's recall is 1.0, so this is a direct comparison.

main_context_reduction.description: Main-context tokens saved against the raw baseline, measured over the items the broker actually brokered. Refused items are excluded from the denominator on purpose: the over-cap item alone is ~88% of the whole-corpus raw baseline, so crediting its counterfactual would make the headline a saving on a payload no lane can answer from. Their raw bytes are reported separately in `refused_raw_bytes`, and the whole-corpus figure is reported too - it is just not what the gate measures.

net_cost_reduction.description: Net total cost including reader input/output and every retry. There is no pricing table in this repository, and inventing one would fake the number, so this stays NOT_RUN even with a live reader until pricing exists.

bounded_latency.description: Per-item wall clock for the deterministic retrieval lane - the only model-free lane that does real work; the raw and legacy lanes are byte arithmetic and would make the bound meaningless. The reader's latency is a provider measurement and belongs to the provider benchmark.

bounded_follow_up_rate.description: How often an answer sends the agent back for another question. Only an answering lane has a follow-up rate.

legacy_compactor.description: The incumbent's shape, fixed here so the comparison cannot drift: keep the first `head_lines`, keep the last `tail_lines`, replace the middle with one elision marker, and stop at `max_bytes`.

items.question: Which downstream dependency did the checkout service report as unavailable, and how many attempts did it make?
What was the last error the service logged before it stopped?
Which process was killed and what limit did it exceed?
What connection pool size did the service start with?
Which exported issue is blocking the release, and who owns it?
Which issue in the export was closed as a duplicate, and of what?
What does the runbook say to do before restarting the queue consumer?
items.expected_quote: Before restarting the consumer, drain the in-flight batch and record the offset.

items.question: Which team is listed as the escalation owner for this component?
items.expected_quote: Escalation owner: team-platform-reliability (rotation shared with team-orders).

items.question: What was the database migration version applied during this window?
Which TLS certificate expired during this window?
What credential did the worker load at startup?
items.note: A realistic cloud journal page can contain a credential marker, and the core refuses to snapshot one at all. That refusal is the designed defence and the strongest available outcome, but it is scored as zero in a denominator that still counts the item - a refusal is a different fact from an answer, reported in its own field.

items.question: What does this oversized journal page say about retries?
items.note: Larger than max_source_bytes. A manifest cannot even declare a size that large - the import contract caps artifact.bytes at the same value - so the refusal is INVALID_REQUEST at the contract boundary rather than a limit hit after reading 8 MiB. The item has no lane that can answer it and scores zero in a counted denominator.
